gaps.sentence: If only I ___ my umbrella — I am getting soaked!
gaps.hint: present regret about an earlier decision
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus the past perfect expresses a present regret about a past decision: had brought.

gaps.sentence: If people ___ less time on their phones, they would read more.
gaps.explanation: An unreal present habit takes the past simple in the if-clause: spent.

gaps.sentence: If the drug ___ tested properly, the side effects would have been found earlier.
gaps.hint: passive verb in an unreal past condition
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect, here in the passive: had been.

gaps.sentence: As long as the budget ___, we can hire two more staff.
gaps.hint: as long as plus a passive condition
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' takes the present simple, here in the passive: is approved.

gaps.sentence: In case of fire, ___ the nearest exit.
gaps.hint: in case of plus an emergency instruction
gaps.explanation: 'In case of' plus a noun introduces an emergency instruction with the imperative: use.

gaps.sentence: If the walls ___ soundproofed, we would not hear the neighbours.
gaps.hint: unreal present with the subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: Unreal present conditions formally take 'were': were.

gaps.sentence: She will be furious if she ___ about this.
gaps.explanation: First conditional: the if-clause stays in the present simple: finds out.

gaps.sentence: ___ there be any problems, call this number.
